Per rules, performance/security practice is usually not applicable for this unit test.

The test method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. It does not follow descriptive naming conventions like methodName_condition_expectedResult, which reduces self-documentation.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are no clear signs of auto-generated verbose code (no 'Auto-generated by...' comments or repetitive test names visible in this single-method snippet). With no evident code-generation artifacts, this practice is not applicable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes a Given-When-Then comment structure and exercises a specific scenario (last index + negative weight), indicating thoughtful design intent and scenario-driven structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API methods (new Grafo, insereAresta, proxAdj) and does not access private fields or use reflection. It verifies observable behavior through public interfaces.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals with expected values) and include descriptive failure messages for many assertions, avoiding generic assertTrue usage and improving diagnosability.

The method contains concise Given-When-Then comments and the class-level Javadoc documents intent; comments explain the scenario rather than the obvious mechanics, so commenting is appropriate and not excessive.
The test contains no uses of Random, current time APIs, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies. It constructs local objects deterministically, so results should be consistent across runs.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates local in-memory objects and does not write files, databases, or modify static/global state in the shown code. No cleanup is necessary for the shown operations, so side effects are avoided.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), which provides categorization metadata to enable selective execution of unit tests.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: One Arrange-Act-Assert improves root-cause. EVALUATION CRITERIA: count distinct Act operations. DECISION: method performs two constructor 'Act' operations (new Grafo(628), new Grafo(1)) and two separate assertions, so >1 Act -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method tests two scenarios in one test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other. RATIONALE: Enables independent execution. EVALUATION: check for shared mutable state or missing setup. DECISION: method uses only local variables and no shared mutable state; no setup/teardown required in method. VERDICT: compliant because the test uses local variables only and does not rely on other tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide happy path and error scenario tests. RATIONALE: Validates robustness. EVALUATION: look for exception tests or class-level multiple tests. DECISION: class contains only this single test method and no exception/invalid-input tests; therefore no coverage of error flows -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is no test for invalid inputs or exceptions and only one test method exists.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundaries (0, negative, max). RATIONALE: Many bugs at boundaries. EVALUATION: look for 0, -1, empty, MAX_VALUE. DECISION: test uses 628 and 1 only; no zero/negative/max tests -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because boundary values such as 0 or negative are not exercised.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication. EVALUATION: look for helper methods/constants or short tests. DECISION: the method is short and does not duplicate across multiple tests; no helper needed. VERDICT: compliant because the test is short and self-contained.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Easier to maintain. EVALUATION: check lines, loops, conditionals. DECISION: method is short (<20 lines) and has linear flow with no loops/complex conditionals. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss faults. EVALUATION: count assertions and property coverage. DECISION: method has two assertions but they verify only a single property (numVertices) for two instances; not verifying multiple properties of a returned object -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because assertions are shallow and do not check additional properties.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored/disabled tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide issues. EVALUATION: look for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION: no @Ignore/@Disabled present and test is active. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Link tests to requirements. RATIONALE: Improves impact analysis. EVALUATION: search for @Story/@Requirement or Javadoc REQ- IDs. DECISION: no requirement annotation or Javadoc linking this test to a requirement -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tested separately. RATIONALE: Unit tests normally don't include them. EVALUATION: look for @Test(timeout=...) or security tests. DECISION: although the method uses a timeout, this is a basic unit assertion; performance/security test practice is typically not applicable for this simple unit test. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should be descriptive. RATIONALE: Names help identify failures. EVALUATION: name patterns like method_scenario_expected. DECISION: method name 'test6' is generic and does not describe scenario or expected outcome -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to non-descriptive name.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose auto-generated tests. RATIONALE: Generated tests can be brittle. EVALUATION: search for auto-generated names/comments. DECISION: presence of EvoRunner/EvoRunnerParameters and generic method name 'test6' suggests generated tests; class comments explicitly mention preserving test0..test8 names -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to signs of code-generation patterns.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD). RATIONALE: Improves maintainability. EVALUATION: look for Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming. DECISION: method contains a 'Given / When / Then' comment in the body indicating design intent. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should exercise public API only. RATIONALE: Avoid brittle tests tied to internals. EVALUATION: search for reflection or private-field access. DECISION: test only calls public constructor and public numVertices(); no reflection/internal access. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Improves failure diagnostics. EVALUATION: look for assertEquals with messages or specific assertions. DECISION: both assertEquals include descriptive messages and specific equality checks. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why'. RATIONALE: Minimal useful comments preferred. EVALUATION: look for commented-out code or excessive comments. DECISION: class and method have concise comments explaining structure and no commented-out code. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid non-determinism. RATIONALE: Prevent flaky tests. EVALUATION: look for Random(), time-based, sleeps. DECISION: method contains none of these constructs and uses local deterministic calls; compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave side effects. RATIONALE: Prevent inter-test dependencies. EVALUATION: search for persisted data or static modifications. DECISION: test uses only local objects and does not persist resources or modify static state in method body. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/tags to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective runs. EVALUATION: look for @Tag/@Category. DECISION: class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class); method inherits classification -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.
